Before I answer, I'll check how your long runs have actually been going. Nothing is logged for your runs or a program yet, so I'm going on general coaching rather than your numbers.

Legs fading in the last mile usually means the long run is a little too fast or too long for where your base is right now. Slow the long run down to a conversational pace and add distance gradually, a bit at a time, and keep most of your weekly miles easy. Two things help a lot: one steady long run each week, and strength work for the legs, like squats, lunges, step-ups and calf raises, once or twice a week. Fueling and sleep the day before matter more than people think.

If you tell me how many days a week you run and what you're training for, I can build you a plan around it. If you'd rather log a few runs first, I can read your pacing and tell you where it's fading.
